newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus market dips, lacks direction.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus market dips, lacks direction.

text.p: Equities on Cyprus's stock exchange closed the week 0.77 percent weaker on Friday in a subdued market lacking direction, market watchers said.
The CSE index fell back 75.12 points on Friday from 75.71 points last week. Cyprus's exchange trades in 89 securities of 43 listed companies.
The market showed declines in the first three trading days of the week, but the trend reversed on Thursday and Friday.

"The market lacks direction. Investors are waiting on the sidelines for some concrete developments on the politcal front," said one trader. "Politics is driving the market," he added, in reference to developments surrounding efforts to reunite the island, divided since Turkey invaded in response to a abortive Greek-led coup on the island in 1974.
Declines during the week were partly technical due to dividend payment by insurance companies, CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation said in a weekly report.
It said its technical analysis pointed to a bearish short term market.

Banking shares fell back 0.16 percent to 83.93 from last week's closing levels. Shares in the Bank of Cyprus (Investments) increased half a cent to 294. Shares of Cyprus Popular Bank fell two cents, to 299.5, and part-dividend shares of the same bank were also trading at 299.5, down one cent from last week.
Shares in Hellenic Bank were trading at 280.5, down 1.5 cents from last week. Universal Bank were trading five cents up at 193.
Insurance company stocks dipped 2.72 percent, with the sub index of the sector falling back to 57.52 points from 59.13 last week.
Universal Life Insurance shares dropped 6.5 cents to close at 455. Fully paid shares in Paneuropean closed at 98.5, two cents lower from last week.
Interamerican Insurance fully paid shares were trading at 87 cents, down 7.5 cents from last week.
Shares in national carrier Cyprus Airways were trading at 34.7 cents from 35 cents last week.
Blue chip cement stocks Vassiliko fully paid closed at 153.5 from 154, and Cyprus Cement were trading at 232 from 234.5 last week.
Beer and wine manufacturer KEO shares closed at 103.5, six cents lower than last week.
Shares of Cyprus Trading Corporation, which this week announced it will seek a listing on the Athens Stock Exchange later this year or in early 1998, were trading at 103.5 from 107.5 last week.
